meta_description: Platform Engineering & Developer Experience from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: How Dataq Software delivers Platform Engineering & Developer Experience — bounded scope, a fixed weekly cadence, the platforms it runs on, and outcomes written into the contract.

Every hour an engineer spends fighting infrastructure is an hour not spent on the product. We build internal developer platforms: golden-path templates (service scaffolding, pipelines, observability, security defaults), a self-service catalog (Backstage-class) with scorecards, environment provisioning in minutes under policy, and a paved road so compelling that the secure path is also the easiest path.

Developer experience is measured, not vibes: DORA metrics (lead time, deployment frequency, change-failure rate, MTTR), onboarding time-to-first-commit, and platform NPS from the engineers themselves. The platform team runs as a product team with a roadmap and a budget — the organizational pattern that separates platforms people adopt from platforms people route around.

Below is the delivery cadence for this capability — the same pattern on every engagement. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
